chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The one who is unconscious (faints) makes up his prayer for three days."

key_terms.الْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The one who is unconscious or has fainted
key_terms.يَقْضِي: Makes up (performs the missed obligatory act)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed prayers after fainting or unconsciousness in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the duration of unconsciousness that exempts a person from prayer, specifying that if one remains in a state of *ghayba* (unconsciousness) for three days, they must perform *qada* (make-up) for those prayers upon regaining consciousness. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between temporary fainting and prolonged unconsciousness, ensuring that the obligation of prayer is neither neglected nor unduly burdened during periods of incapacitation.
